answer: A Registered domain bound by DNS record proof with one identity per channel ties the identity to something the applicant actually controls: the registered domain answers a fresh challenge, the DNS record proof is recorded, and one identity per channel keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a Sybil farm would need a separate real channel for every fake account. A sonnet that appears twice is the tell: the same channel cannot back two identities. Between a lotus and a fable lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to bind.
